name: Chris Bane

tenures.source: The promotion's own on-screen Commissioner throughout its 17 June 1999 broadcast, engineering a rival's loss by revenge interference to hand the vacant Tradition Championship to Prophet.

The promotion's on-screen commissioner, who awarded the vacated Cruiserweight Championship to Jarry Rice by decree and named himself special guest referee for the following week's number-one contender's match.

caption: A commissioner who used one night in charge to hand out a Cruiserweight Championship and name himself special referee.

name: Dan Davidson

tenures.source: Wrestled Prophet in a first-round Tradition Title tournament match on the promotion's own 17 June 1999 broadcast, losing by submission to a figure-four leglock.
Tackled a rival off a police car in the Hardcore battle royal before being eliminated by Cryptic Saber's reverse DDT and a section of steel fence.

caption: A Hardcore Championship battle royal entrant whose own football tackle off a police car couldn't save him from Cryptic Saber.

name: "Dangerous" Dan Santos

tenures.source: A color commentator, billed "Dangerous" Dan Santos, on the promotion's 17 June 1999 broadcast.
A color commentator across both of the promotion's surviving broadcasts.

caption: A color commentator whose Hawaiian shirt and needling of his broadcast partners were a running bit of both surviving shows.

name: "The Rocket" Jarry Rice

tenures.source: Appeared on the promotion's own 17 June 1999 broadcast as a squash-match victim of Wild Thing and Kyle Brentwood.
Was awarded the vacated Cruiserweight Championship by decree after its champion's retirement, then lost the title to a masked challenger in a mask-versus-title match.

caption: A Cruiserweight Champion crowned by decree rather than by a match, unmasked no one but lost his own title in a mask-versus-title stipulation two weeks later.

name: Joe Eckert

tenures.source: The promotion's own founding president throughout its held record; attacked by a rival ("Sweetness") during the 17 June 1999 broadcast before a newly-debuting wrestler came to his aid.
The promotion's own president, absent from its first served broadcast; its commissioner announced he had left him in charge for the night.

caption: The promotion's own founding president, whose absence from its opening broadcast left a subordinate to make its first title decision.

name: Lance Mayson

tenures.source: The promotion's ring announcer on its 17 June 1999 broadcast.
The promotion's ring announcer across both of its surviving broadcasts.

caption: The promotion's own ring announcer for the whole of its surviving record.

name: "The All American" Mark Jones

tenures.source: Debuted on the promotion's own 17 June 1999 broadcast as the newest member of the stable Razor's From Dollywood, arriving after an on-screen attack on the promotion's own president.
Lost the promotion's opening match to Alec "The Destroyer" Empire after nearly winning with his own top-rope finisher, The Fourth of July.

caption: A red-white-and-blue patriot gimmick whose near-win off the top rope wasn't quite enough on opening night.

name: Mike Holmes

tenures.source: Named as one of the promotion's newly-signed wrestlers, billed "Hard Rock" Mike Holmes, in its own 2 May 1999 recruitment update; no match result survives in this held record.
Wrestled disguised as an unnamed masked man and won the Cruiserweight Championship from Jarry Rice with the help of a second masked accomplice, unmasking afterward to a returning wrestler's ovation.

caption: A returning wrestler who won back the Cruiserweight Championship under a mask, with a fellow masked returnee helping from ringside.

name: Prophet

tenures.source: Won a first-round Tradition Title tournament match over "Dollywood" Dan Davidson on the promotion's own 17 June 1999 broadcast, then won the vacant Tradition Championship outright the same night after the Commissioner's own on-screen interference against a rival.
Eliminated a rival in the Hardcore battle royal atop a police car, then helped Oracle win the World Tag Team Championship from the Too Cool Connection by making the winning cover himself.

caption: A member of the stable Razor's From Dollywood whose own pinfall, set up by his tag partner's interference, won the World Tag Team Championship.

identity.note: Shares a name with two already-held wrestlers of the same name in other wings; nothing in this promotion's own record states an operator or history connecting any of them.

name: Razor

tenures.source: Billed as the promotion's own Tradition Champion entering its 17 June 1999 broadcast, having upset the Hardcore Champion the week before, then vacating the Tradition Title on-screen rather than relinquish the Hardcore Title.
Billed as the reigning WWWA World Heavyweight Champion throughout this record, appearing at ringside to support his own stable's Cruiserweight challenger.

caption: A stable leader billed as the promotion's own World Heavyweight Champion for the whole of this record, never shown defending the title in a structured match.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (razor-cwo); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (razor-wewf); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: Sandy Karsen

tenures.source: A lead commentator on the promotion's 17 June 1999 broadcast.
A lead commentator across both of the promotion's surviving broadcasts.

caption: A lead broadcast commentator across the whole of the promotion's surviving record.

name: "The Suicide Machine" Tommy Jobber

tenures.source: The promotion's own Hardcore Champion entering its 17 June 1999 broadcast; upset for the vacated Tradition Title by Razor there, and injured badly enough by Razor's own finisher to be, in the broadcast's own words, "sidelined for a couple of months."
A former Hardcore Champion who returned for the eight-man battle royal that crowned the promotion's newly-renamed Hardcore Championship, eliminating two rivals before being eliminated himself.

caption: A returning former Hardcore Champion whose comeback battle royal run ended just short of a second title.

identity.note: Shares a name with an already-held wrestler of the same name in another wing; nothing in this promotion's own record states an operator or history connecting the two.
